1.1.label = Intro 1.1.alert.modal = The rifle grenade can add a strong tactical element to any assault, particularly against infantry behind cover. Along with being much more accurate than hand-thrown grenades, rifle grenades can be projected to a much greater distance.
1.2.label = Grenadier Role in an Assault Team 1.2.alert.modal = Remember, it takes more than one soldier to win a battle. Fulfilling your role in a team can make the difference between an overwhelming victory and a disaster. Firing one or two grenades into a bunker can kill the defenders or disorient them enough for a submachine gunner to move in and clear it out.
1.3.label = Types of Rifle Grenades 1.3.alert.modal = It is important to take note of the type of rifle grenades available to each army.
1.4.label = The British Rifle Grenade 1.4.alert.modal = The British rifle grenade is a High Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT) grenade which detonates on impact. The HEAT grenade is most useful against trucks and light armored vehicles.
1.5.label = The French Rifle Grenade 1.5.alert.modal = The French rifle grenade is a High Explosive (HE) grenade which detonates on an eight second fuse. This HE grenade is most useful against enemy infantry in a fortified position.
1.6.label = The German Rifle Grenade 1.6.alert.modal = The German rifle grenade is a High Explosive (HE) grenade which detonates on impact. This HE grenade is useful both against fortified and mobile enemy infantry.
1.7.label = Firing Position 1.7.alert = Move forward to the firing line. #waypoint label: "Firing Line" #waypoint: -314046.56,3603720.08,101.73
1.8.label = Attaching the Grenade Launcher Cup 1.8.alert = The rifle grenade requires the grenade launcher cup to be attached for use. Attach the cup by pressing {fpdeploy}.
1.9.label = Loading the Rifle Grenade 1.9.alert = Attaching the cup disables normal rifle use until the cup is removed. Once the cup is attached, press {fpreload} to load a rifle grenade. 1.9.complete.modal = Once a grenade is loaded, the cup cannot be removed until the grenade has been deployed. Be sure to only load a rifle grenade when you are ready to use it.
1.10.label = Aiming the Rifle Grenade 1.10.alert.modal = The rifle grenade must be held at an appropriate angle to fire correctly. This prevents use of the rifle’s iron sights while aiming. As with hand-thrown grenades, be aware of the arc of the grenade when aiming.
1.11.label = Firing the Rifle Grenade 1.11.alert = Now aim at one of the targets on the range and fire the grenade by pressing {fpfire}.
1.12.label = Firing the Rifle Grenade (cont.) 1.12.alert.modal = The grenade cup holds only one grenade at a time, requiring a new round to be loaded after each shot with {fpreload} to fire more grenades.
1.13.label = Resupply 1.13.alert = When you are done firing at the targets, resupply at the supply truck or halftrack.[NL][NL]You may resupply at any point during this tutorial. #waypoint label: "Supply Truck" #waypoint: -314010.18, 3603738.84, 102
1.14.label = Removing the Grenade Launcher Cup 1.14.alert.modal = Normal bullets cannot be fired while the cup is attached. To resume normal rifle use, you must press {fpdeploy} to remove the cup. # this should be just a reminder, and let them leave the cup on
2.0.label = Vehicles and Buildings
2.1.label = Damaging Vehicles 2.1.alert = The rifle grenade is very effective against unarmored and lightly armored vehicles such as trucks and haulers. It is also useful against infantry in buildings.[NL][NL]Move to the Vehicle Target Range. #waypoint label "Vehicle Target Range" #waypoint: -313969.40,3603763.17,100.32
2.2.label = Practice Firing on Vehicles 2.2.alert = Practice firing at the vehicles with your rifle grenades by pressing {fpfire}. 2.2.complete.modal = Great work soldier! This completes your grenadier training. Feel free to practice as long as you like. For extra practice try to fire a grenade through a door or window in the building to your right.
content.brief: This tutorial introduces you to the rifle grenade launcher.
